subject: Subprocessor swap in-flight — UK Addendum acceptance and evidence
messages:
From: Sarah Hunter <sarah.hunter@lumenhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com, privacy@lumenhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 14:14:00 +0000
Subject: Notice: subprocessor swap and UK addendum acceptance

Hi Chloe / Jonas,

Quick heads up — Lumen is planning to transition a third-party inference cache provider (CacheWave Ltd) to replace one of your currently-declared subprocessors for EU-based traffic. Procurement requested a short confirmation that Redwood will:

- accept the UK Addendum / IDTA language for the new subprocessor (we operate under a UK jurisdiction subset for some products)
- provide the TIA/DTIA evidence bucket or mapping for us to attach to our records

Attached is a two-tab summary of the proposed swap (subprocessor_swap_summary.xlsx) with the expected cutover window (Nov 10–13). Our legal and privacy teams need explicit confirmation that the UK Addendum redline shared previously covers this new subprocessor or, if not, when Redwood can provide a documented exception/attestation.

Can you confirm by EOD Thursday 23 Oct? If you prefer a short call, happy to do 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Hunter
Sr. Procurement Manager, Lumen Health
--
Attachment: subprocessor_swap_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Hunter <sarah.hunter@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 16:02:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Notice: subprocessor swap and UK addendum acceptance

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the spreadsheet. We're tracking the cutover window and I'll coordinate internally. Two quick notes from our side:

1) UK Addendum: our standard UK Addendum language is consistent across subprocessors, but we maintain a short exception attestation for new providers that handle ephemeral cache data. I'll get legal to confirm whether CacheWave is covered by the existing redline or needs an explicit addendum execution.

2) Evidence/TIA: we can provide the DTIA mapping and a scoped evidence bundle (logs retention, egress controls, and subprocessors list) for the cutover. We'll need to redact any internal IPs.

Kimberly — can you confirm the UK Addendum status for CacheWave and whether we should escalate to signatory for a counter-signed addendum? Markus — FYI on potential SLA/ops impact for the switchover window. Jonas — you'll likely coordinate customer communications.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0133

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Hunter <sarah.hunter@lumenhealth.com>, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 09:30:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Notice: subprocessor swap and UK addendum acceptance

Chloe / team / Sarah — I reviewed CacheWave's profile and the UK Addendum redline (attached: uk_addendum_redline_v2.pdf). Quick summary:

- Contracting: CacheWave meets our standard subprocessor security baseline but is not currently named in the master DPA; therefore, we will treat this as an in-scope subprocessor onboarding.
- UK Addendum: the language in uk_addendum_redline_v2 is appropriate for CacheWave from a data transfer perspective. However, Lumen's requirement for an explicit IDTA attestation means we need to provide a short signed Certificate of Processing that references CacheWave and confirms our routing safeguards (TIA mapping).
- Evidence: we can assemble a DTIA packet with encrypted logs (sample), retention policy excerpt, and a signed subprocessor questionnaire. That packet will be suitable for your records.

Next steps I propose:
- We produce the signed Certificate of Processing (internal legal signatory) and a DTIA evidence bundle by Fri 24 Oct EOD.
- If Lumen needs a countersigned UK Addendum, we can route a partner-execution DocuSign (low-labor — 1–2 business days).
- Technical ops: we should run a dry swap in our staging environment on Nov 3–4. Markus, can you confirm ops availability?

If that plan is acceptable, Sarah, we'll mark deliverables on Friday and the DocuSign link will follow only if you request countersignature.

Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
--
Attachment: uk_addendum_redline_v2.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

From: Sarah Hunter <sarah.hunter@lumenhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Fri, 24 Oct 2025 11:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Notice: subprocessor swap and UK addendum acceptance

Chloe / Kimberly — this plan works for us. Thank you for the swift review. Two final asks before we mark procurement green:

1) Please upload the DTIA evidence bundle to the Drive link you referenced and share access to privacy@lumenhealth.com.
2) If you are planning a signed Certificate of Processing, include the exact processor name and the effective date range; Lumen needs the effective date to match the Nov 10 cutover.

We'll standby for the bundle by EOD Friday and will confirm the procurement queue once we see the signed attestation. If anything slips, please alert procurement immediately so we can hold the cutover window.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Hunter
Sr. Procurement Manager, Lumen Health
--
Reply thread: Chloe confirmed with Kimberly that the DTIA packet and Certificate of Processing will be provided and Drive link will be shared. Next operational coordination to follow with Markus for staging dates.
